title: Rapid and Reliable Excitation Wavelength-Dependent Detection of 2,6-Dipicolinic Acid Based on a Luminescent Cd(II)–Tb(III) Nanocluster

material_class.structural_family: Cd10Tb9 nanocluster with two crystallographically independent components

synthesis.procedure: Tb(OAc)3·6H2O (0.20 mmol, 0.065 g), Cd(OAc)2·4H2O (0.20 mmol, 0.049 g), and HL (0.20 mmol, 0.033 g) were dissolved in EtOH (6 mL) and MeOH (4 mL), followed by addition of trimethylamine in 1 mL of MeOH (c = 1.0 mol/L). After refluxing for 30 min with stirring, the mixture was filtered. The filtrate was diffused slowly by diethyl ether for 3 weeks, forming a yellow crystalline product. The crystals were filtered off and washed with 5 mL of EtOH three times. Lanthanide compounds were synthesized using a Schlenk system.

reagents.name: trimethylamine
reagents.amount: 1 mL of MeOH solution, c = 1.0 mol/L

synthesis.time: reflux 30 min with stirring; diethyl ether diffusion 3 weeks
synthesis.vessel_or_method: Schlenk system; reflux then filtration and diethyl ether vapor diffusion
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Filtered after reflux; filtrate slowly diffused with diethyl ether for 3 weeks to give yellow crystals; crystals filtered off and washed with 5 mL EtOH three times.

properties.summary: 1 shows ligand-sensitized Tb(III) emission and excitation-wavelength-dependent luminescence sensing of DPA: enhancement at λex = 272 nm (LOD 0.23 nM) and quenching at λex = 329 nm (KSV = 0.029 μM−1, LOD 6.17 μM). The intensity ratio IEx272nm/IEx329nm follows a second-order equation usable for quantitative DPA assay in CH3CN and tap water. Response is <5 s, photostable over 24 h, and selective versus aromatic carboxylates, amino acids, and common ions. Lifetimes (~1.8–1.9 ms) are essentially unchanged upon DPA addition, consistent with a static process. Test papers of 1 detect DPA by green emission under a UV lamp.
